The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

The banner the reporter circled on nove3cinco.pt is the site's own first-party ad inventory:⁠ a publisher-hosted sponsor carousel (div#⁠banner, slides linking to froiz.pt and six other advertisers) with creatives on nove3cinco.pt's own uploads and no ad network request anywhere in the page's traffic. The repository policy that the site's own first-party advertising is not deliberately blocked therefore calls for recommending close rather than a rule.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction filter policy:⁠ "The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing." The reporter-defined target is a first-party ad served by the publisher itself, so the fix is blocked by this rule rather than by missing evidence. KnowledgeBase filter policy (served via lookup_rule_guidance):⁠ "The site's own advertising should not be deliberately blocked. However, it should not be unblocked if the blocking is caused by general filtering rules." A dedicated rule for this banner would deliberately block it; the banner is not blocked by any general rule today (get_applied_rules shows only four Tracking Protection scriptlets acting on the page). The report is not anti-adblock, not a paywall and not a scam/phishing page, so none of the other policy bullets applies; only the first-party-advertising bullet governs it.
